modules.behavior: AXI4-Lite slave write side: AW, W and B channels driving a register-bank write port. Byte addresses are 6 bits; awaddr[5] = 1 (0x20..0x3F) is out of range, awaddr[1:0] are ignored and the register index is awaddr[4:2]. State: aw_full with aw_addr[5:0]; w_full with w_data[31:0] and w_strb[3:0]; bvalid with bresp[1:0]; all reset to 0. Every output is a view of that state with no combinational path from any input: awready = !aw_full and wready = !w_full (the channels are independent; neither ready waits for the other channel's valid); bvalid and bresp are the registers; with do_write = aw_full && w_full && !bvalid, wr_en = do_write && !aw_addr[5]; wr_idx = aw_addr[4:2], wr_data = w_data and wr_strb = w_strb are shown whatever wr_en is. At each rising edge with rst low, using the state and inputs before the edge: if do_write then aw_full = 0, w_full = 0, bvalid = 1 and bresp = 2 (SLVERR) when aw_addr[5] = 1, else 0 (OKAY); the bank writes at this same edge, so the register update and the response become visible together, and an out-of-range write changes no register. Otherwise, if bvalid && bready then bvalid = 0. Independently, if awvalid && awready then aw_full = 1 and aw_addr = awaddr; if wvalid && wready then w_full = 1, w_data = wdata and w_strb = wstrb. So AW and W may arrive in either order or together, one of each may be held while a response is pending, and a held pair is written only at an edge where bvalid was 0 before the edge (not at the edge where a stalled response retires). A write costs at least two edges, so one write per two cycles is the peak rate. bresp keeps its value after the B transfer. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: axil_wr_if

modules.behavior: Bank of eight 32-bit registers behind one write port, exposed as a flat 256-bit view. Map by index (byte address 4*index): 0 CTRL read/write, reset 0, also driven on output ctrl; 1 SCRATCH read/write, reset 0; 2 CONFIG read/write, reset 0x00000100; 3 IRQ_MASK: bits 7:0 read/write, written only when wr_strb[0] = 1, bits 31:8 read 0, reset 0; 4 IRQ_STATUS: bits 7:0 pending flags, write-1-to-clear, bits 31:8 read 0, reset 0; 5 STATUS read-only: status_in as sampled at the previous rising edge (registered every cycle), reset 0; 6 ID read-only constant 0x52544C35; 7 WRITE_COUNT read-only: the number of edges with wr_en = 1 since reset (any index, any strobes), modulo 2^32, reset 0. regs_flat[32*i+31:32*i] = register i, ctrl = CTRL and irq = OR of the bits of (IRQ_STATUS[7:0] & IRQ_MASK[7:0]); all three depend only on registered state. At each rising edge with rst low, using pre-edge values: STATUS = status_in; IRQ_STATUS[7:0] = (IRQ_STATUS[7:0] & ~clear) | irq_set, where clear = wr_data[7:0] if wr_en && wr_idx == 4 && wr_strb[0], else 0, so a flag that is set and cleared at the same edge stays set; if wr_en then WRITE_COUNT increments, for index 0, 1 or 2 each byte lane b with wr_strb[b] = 1 takes byte b of wr_data and the other lanes keep their value, and for index 3 IRQ_MASK[7:0] = wr_data[7:0] when wr_strb[0] = 1; writes to indexes 5, 6 and 7 change nothing but still count. When wr_en = 0, wr_idx, wr_data and wr_strb are ignored. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.
modules.name: axil_regbank

modules.behavior: AXI4-Lite slave read side: AR and R channels reading a flat view of eight 32-bit registers, where regs_flat[32*i+31:32*i] is register i. Byte addresses are 6 bits; araddr[5] = 1 (0x20..0x3F) is out of range, araddr[1:0] are ignored and the index is araddr[4:2]. State rvalid, rdata[31:0] and rresp[1:0], all reset to 0; arready = !rvalid, from registered state only. At each rising edge with rst low: if arvalid && !rvalid the read is accepted: rvalid = 1 and, when araddr[5] = 1, rdata = 0 and rresp = 2 (SLVERR), else rdata = register araddr[4:2] of regs_flat as it was before this edge and rresp = 0 (OKAY); otherwise, if rvalid && rready then rvalid = 0. While rvalid && !rready, rvalid, rdata and rresp hold whatever arvalid, araddr or regs_flat do, and rdata and rresp keep their values after the R transfer. The next read can be accepted at the edge after an R transfer at the earliest. Synchronous active-high rst at a rising edge returns every register to its reset value; reset has no effect between edges. Python oracle: cycle-level model, one step per rising edge; keep the registers in state and return every output as it is after that edge. The driver applies the fixed latency of 1; do not add a delay queue. init() is the reset state and a supplied rst must be handled.

implementation.meaning: Out-of-context implementation (chip_top_flow_for_soc_block): the top is a block inside a larger design, synthesized with synth_design -mode out_of_context and placed and routed without I/O buffers or package pins. clk is constrained at the target period and modeled as driven by a global clock buffer (HD.CLK_SRC). Data ports have no input or output delay and no pad delay, so they are unconstrained I/O; the routed WNS and WHS, and timing acceptance, cover the internal clocked paths only, and combinational logic between a port and its first or last register is not timed. Utilization excludes I/O buffers.

metric_provenance: Structured metrics are parsed from retained reports; routed utilization/timing reports take precedence when present. The manifest identifies complete files by hash. Header excerpts are bounded previews, not complete reports or an independent metric source.
objective_policy: First establish timing feasibility. A verified timing-feasible candidate may replace a known timing-infeasible previous best even with higher area or power; classify this as timing_recovery, not objective savings. While the previous best is timing-infeasible, a verified still-infeasible candidate with strictly better setup WNS and hold not worse beyond a small tolerance may replace it as timing_progress, which is not closure; a feasible candidate always outranks it. Once both are timing-feasible, require strict improvement of the chosen objective; for maximize_freq that is register-to-register setup slack (reg2reg_wns_ns) when both designs report it, otherwise full setup WNS for both, while feasibility stays on full WNS and WHS. minimize_luts compares (lut_used, ff_used) and minimize_ffs compares (ff_used, lut_used) lexicographically: an equal primary metric with a strictly lower secondary is an objective improvement, a higher primary never is, and a secondary missing from either design gives no tie-break. Unknown or contradictory incumbent timing evidence cannot establish recovery. A completed experiment may find no improvement. Do not invent mandatory savings, slack margins, tool versions, timing corners, new tests, thresholds, code-style quotas or external environment requirements.
